- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices during early recovery phases after sharp drops; model lags in recognizing rebound momentum.
- Exhibit persistent bias toward higher prices when recent 30-day average is above 70; model consistently overpredicts.
- Underreact to downward trends in the last 5–7 days; model fails to adjust downward quickly when recent prices are falling.
- Overfit to recent volatility; model amplifies noise in price swings rather than smoothing toward mean.
- When true outcome is below forecast by >5%, model often fails to correct in next 3–5 days; suggest downward revision with lagged smoothing.
- Model tends to overestimate mid-range prices (65–75) and underestimates extremes (below 65 or above 75) — apply asymmetric scaling for edge cases.
- Avoid extrapolating from single-day spikes; model often misinterprets short-term volatility as sustained trend.
